World Cup Fever: NY Puts $10 Million into Youth Soccer

Jana DeakPublished: November 24, 2026
  • Share on Facebook
  • Share on Twitter

The 2026 FIFA World Cup may be over, but New York is making sure the soccer fever sticks around.

Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 1:35
Instaread

Governor Kathy Hochul announced Monday that New York State is investing more than $10 million to expand youth soccer access, using the momentum from this summer's World Cup to fund new fields, upgrades and youth programs across the state.

The biggest piece is a $5.5 million project in Central Park, which will transform a large parking lot near Tavern on the Green into a publicly accessible mini soccer pitch and community space.

Another nearly $5 million will go to 30 projects through the NY KICKS program, including several right here in the Hudson Valley. Kingston, Montgomery, Newburgh, Ossining, Rhinebeck and other communities will receive funding for new fields, lighting, renovations and expanded soccer facilities.

And if you're wondering why New York is putting so much emphasis on soccer right now, remember who we had representing us on the world's biggest stage.

Wappingers Falls native Tyler Adams was part of the U.S. Men's National Team at this year's World Cup, helping the Americans reach the Round of 16. Adams grew up playing soccer in Dutchess County and now has the Tyler Adams Soccer Pitch named in his honor at Martz Field in Wappingers Falls.

Prominent Professional Athletes from The Hudson Valley Region

We've compiled a list of 25 male professional athletes who are from the Hudson Valley.

Gallery Credit: William Smith

Al Bello/Getty Images

Andre Williams - Poughkeepsie, NY

Born in Poughkeepsie, Williams is no stranger to giving back. Soon after he was drafted by the New York Giants in 2014. He started a foundation called the “Get Schooled foundation” talking to kids in high school, college, and athletes instilling in them how important their education is, and to always bet on themselves. 

Steph Chambers/Getty Images

Elijah Hughes - Poughkeepsie, NY

Born March 10th, 1998 in Poughkeepsie, New York. Hughes grew up in Beacon, he started playing basketball through his Catholic Youth Organization (CYO) and soon after began playing on the (AAU) circuit for a local coach of his, Kenny Dawson. Hughes became well known in the area for his talent and dominating games at Loopers Park. He went on to attend East Carolina, South Kent, and Syracuse Universities.

Jonathan Daniel/Getty Images

Patrick Whearty - Poughkeepsie, NY

Born August 27th, 1980 Patrick Whearty grew up in Poughkeepsie, New York. He attended Our Lady of Lourdes High School and went on to attend the College of Holy Cross. Only noticed because of a call his mother made to Holy Cross’s coach, he ended up playing Center there from 1998-2003, he went on to play professionally overseas from 2003-2008 before retiring.

Photo by NFL via Getty Images

Rashad Barksdale - Hudson, NY

Born May 11, 1984 he grew up in Hudson, NY where he also attended High School. After High School he went onto play football at the University of Albany. He led the Great Danes in interceptions and punt returns in 2006, before going onto the NFL Draft the following year. He was drafted by the Philidelphia Eagles in the 6th round (201st overall). He is the second player in school history to be drafted into the NFL.

Harry How/Getty Images

Hilton Armstrong - Peekskill, NY

Playing for Peekskill High School before moving onto UConn Men's basketball from 2002-2006, a former lottery pick of the 2006 NBA draft serves as a role model for many from his hometown. For him, his NBA journey did not go as expected. Playing for almost ten teams, even at 30 years old he still would ride his bike to the arena with a smile on his face, knowing how lucky he was to even have the opportunity to be doing something most dream of.

Euroleague Basketball via Getty Images

Mike Tobey - Monroe, NY

Born October 10th, 1994 after attending Monroe Woodbury Middle School, Tobey attended Blair Academy, where he averaged 21 points and nine rebounds. He was a Top 100 Recruit by ESPN. He wore number 10 in high school and college because he was born on October 10 at 10 a.m. and weighed 10 pounds at birth. Coming from a family full of athletes his dad, Ken Sr. played basketball at St. Thomas Aquinas College.

Matt Hazlett/Getty Images

Pierre Garcon - Carmel, NY

Born August 8, 1986 grew up in Carmel Hamlet, NY. He went on to attend Mount Union College, eventually getting drafted in 2008, round 6, pick 205 to the Indianapolis Colts.

Photo by NFL via Getty Images

Ryan Williams - Cold Spring, NY

Born April 9, 1990 is a former NFL running back. Born in Cold Spring, NY he went onto play collegiate and professional football. In college he played for Virginia Tech and on January 9, 2011, it was announced that Williams will give up his final 2 years of NCAA eligibility to make himself available for the 2011 NFL Draft.

Mike Ehrmann/Getty Images

Ali Marpet - Hastings-On-Hudson, NY

Born April 17th, 1993 in Hastings On the Hudson. He attended Hastings High School, playing both offensive tackle and defensive end for the Yellowjackets. He was a three-time varsity letterman, named second team All-State, earned all-section honors, and was a two-time all-league selection. He played the offensive line as a 160 pounds (73 kg) ninth-grader. Marpet quit playing football after his freshman year to focus on basketball where he earned all-league selection twice. Marpet rejoined the football team in his junior year, by which time he weighed 210 pounds (95 kg). Marpet helped lead the Hastings squad to the section finals in 2010. Hastings lost to Bronxville, the eventual state champions.

Julio Aguilar/Getty Images

Joe Giles Harris - Nyack, NY

Born April 1, 1997 grew up in Nyack, NY. He went on to fulfill a lifelong dream of playing in the NFL. He went on to play for Duke University and entered the NFL draft in 2019, going undrafted, signed with the Jacksonville Jaguars.

Rob Carr/Getty Images

Terrence Fede - Nyack, NY

Born to Haitian parents, on November 19th 1991, they lived in Nyack, New York. Fede attended Nyack High School in Upper Nyack, as a dual athlete, playing football and basketball. He went on to play College Football at Marist College. Fede was the first player from Marist College to be drafted. Fede totaled 13 sacks his senior season, and 31 for his college career. In 2013, he was named PFL Defensive Player of the Year, First Team All-PFL, 6th in voting for Buck Buchanan Award, selected All-American by five separate outlets, and two-time PFL Defensive Player of the Week. He totaled 13 sacks, and led the FCS in sacks per game, broke program records for sacks in a season (13) and career (30.5), and was the first player in program history to win major award from the PFL.

Jason Miller/Getty Images

Kevin Huerter - Albany, NY

Born August 27th, 1998. Kevin Huerter grew up in Clifton Park, New York, a suburb of Albany located in Saratoga County. Standing at 6’7, Huerter played shooting guard for the Shenendehowa High School basketball team. During his time, there he led the school to its second state championship, set the state scoring record and, as a senior, was named Mr. New York Basketball. He currently plays for the Atlanta Hawks of the NBA.

Photo by NFL Photos

Adam Terry - Glenn Falls, NY

Born September 1, 1982 he is now 38 years of age. Growing up in Queensbury, NY he attended his local High School. As a junior he was a first team All-Conference pick and a first team All-State selection, and was named on All-East selection by Prep Football Report.

Dave Sandford/Getty Images

Matt Murley - Troy, NY

Born December 17, 1979 Matt grew up in Troy, NY. In his youth, Murley played in the 1993 Quebec International Pee-Wee Hockey Tournament with a major ice hockey team from Syracuse, New York. In college, he played hockey for four seasons at the Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute in his hometown. In the 1999 NHL Entry Draft, he was drafted in the 2nd round (51st overall) by the Pittsburgh Penguins.

Elsa Hasch/Getty Images

Guy Hebert - Troy, NY

Born January 7, 1967 former professional ice hockey goaltender grew up in Troy, NY. He is a graduate of La Salle Institute in Troy and Hamilton College in Clinton, NY. He played for the New York Rangers during his pro career and is now an associate host on Fox Sports Prime ticket.

Photo by NFL via Getty Images

Courtney Greene - New Rochelle, NY

Born November 23, 1986 Greene grew up in New Rochelle, NY. He starred at New Rochelle High School alongside future college teammates Ray Rice and Glenroy Lee. He led New Rochelle to the Class AA state championship in 2003, in which he earned MVP honors. Greene played a prep year during te 2004 season at Bridgton Academy.

Jonathan Daniel/Getty Images

Ray Rice - New Rochelle, NY

New Rochelle's native, Ray Rice played for the Baltimore Ravens during his professional career from (2008-2013). In 2017 he returned to his old high school as a running backs coach. Playing for the school from 2001-2004, he brought them a state championship in 2003. With his professional experience, he aims to give back to the kids who are growing up in the place he has always known and loved to be home.  

Jonathan Daniel/Getty Images

Elton Brand - Cortlandt Manor, NY

Born March 11th, 1979 grew up in Cortlandt Manor, New York. Brand attended and played basketball at Peekskill High School, where he was immediately implemented into the Varisty basketball roster. During his high school career, he averaged 40 points and 20 rebounds per game, played AAU with future NBA players Lamar Odom and Ron Artest. By his senior year was consistently ranked as one of the best players in the country, being selected as Mr. New York Basketball.

J Meric/Getty Images

Kevin Jones - Mount Vernon

Born August 25, 1989 was born in Mount Vernon, NY. He attended Mount Vernon High School in Mount Vernon. As a junior he averaged 21 points, 12 rebounds, and two blocks per game. As a senior, he averaged 23 points, 14 rebounds, and two blocks per game. In 2006 and 2007, he led Mount Vernon to the New York State PHSAA championships.

Gregory Shamus/Getty Images

Andre Drummond - Mount Vernon, NY

Born August 10th, 1993 in Mount Vernon, New York. Born to Jamaican parents and his sister they moved out of the Hudson Valley at the age of 7. He always kept his roots close to him, going onto to play at the University of Connecticut, and now known as one of the more dominant centers in the NBA.

Jason Miller/Getty Images

Channing Frye - White Plains, NY

Seven-footer Channing Frye is more than just an NBA player. In 2007, Frye established The Channing Frye Foundation. The foundation was founded with the goal of pointing youth in a positive and healthy direction. In 2010, Frye and his wife established The Frye Family Foundation in order to give back to the communities that are important to the Frye's.

Michael Reaves/Getty Images

Sean Kilpatrick - Yonkers, NY

Born January 6th, 1990 in Yonkers, New York played his high school basketball at White Plains Senior High School. He averaged 28.4 points, 7 rebounds, and 6 assists per game over his four-year career. He went onto play college, professional, and overseas professionally as well.

Jonathan Daniel/Getty Images

Nate Collins - White Plains, NY

White Plains native, has played on many teams over the course of his NFL career. In April 2011, Collins and New York Giants receiver Victor Cruz started the clothing brand, Young Whales. The line, a play on words of a high-stakes casino gambler "whale", was ready for purchase online by September 2011. Coming from White Plains and playing 4 seasons in the NFL is something not most can say they have done.

Jamie Squire/Getty Images

Jordan Lucas - White Plains, NY

27-year-old Superbowl champion with the Kansas City Chiefs. His mother credits White Plains for making him into the man he is today. Brother-in-law of former NFL star running back Ray Rice, Lucas is very active in giving back. He makes donations to various foundations while helping peaceful protestors get out of jail, which has had a profound impact on the community, and serves as a role model for the younger generation in White Plains.

Matt Szwajkos, Alan Taylor/Getty Images

Tommy Boggs - Poughkeepsie, NY

Tommy Boggs is one of about 10 people to ever make it to the MLB from Poughkeepsie. Talk about putting your town on the map? Drafted in 1974, he played 9 years in the MLB. Boggs serves as a role model for those also from Poughkeepsie that they can live out their life long dreams the way he was able to.

10 Most Famous and Iconic Trophies in Sports History

Explore the world's 10 most iconic sports trophies, from the Stanley Cup and Vince Lombardi Trophy to the FIFA World Cup, Wimbledon hardware, and the Claret Jug.

Gallery Credit: Michaela Johnson

Getty Images

Heisman Trophy: College Football's Top Individual Award

Cast in solid bronze, the Heisman Memorial Trophy depicts a football player executing a stiff-arm and serves as college football's top individual honor.

Getty Images

The Stanley Cup: NHL Hockey Championship Trophy History

First awarded in 1893, the Stanley Cup is North America's oldest professional sports trophy, featuring hand-engraved names of every winning player.

Getty Images

Vince Lombardi Trophy: Super Bowl Championship Award

Crafted from sterling silver by Tiffany & Co., the Vince Lombardi Trophy stands 22 inches tall and represents the ultimate prize in professional football.

Getty Images

FIFA World Cup Trophy: History & Value of Soccer's Top Prize

Sculpted from 18-karat gold with a malachite base, the 14-pound FIFA World Cup Trophy depicts two human figures holding up the Earth.

Getty Images

Larry O'Brien Trophy: NBA Finals Championship Award

Standing 2 feet tall and crafted from 24-karat gold vermeil over sterling silver, the Larry O'Brien Trophy depicts a basketball about to enter a net.

Getty Images

Commissioner's Trophy: MLB World Series Championship Award

Featuring 30 gold-plated flags representing each Major League team, the sterling silver Commissioner's Trophy honors the World Series champion.

Getty Images

Kentucky Derby Trophy: Solid Gold Horse Racing Prize

Handcrafted from 14-karat solid gold at Churchill Downs, the Kentucky Derby Trophy is one of the few solid gold awards in modern professional sports.

Getty Images

Borg-Warner Trophy: Indy 500 Motorsport Championship Prize

Standing nearly 5 feet tall and weighing over 110 pounds, the silver Borg-Warner Trophy features sculpted sterling silver faces of every Indy 500 winner.

Getty Images

Wimbledon Trophies: Men's Cup & Women's Rosewater Dish

Presented since the 1880s, the Gentlemen's Singles silver-gilt cup and the Ladies' Singles sterling silver Venus Rosewater Dish serve as tennis's top Grand Slam prizes.

Getty Images

The Claret Jug: Golf's Open Championship Silver Trophy

Officially named the Golf Champion Trophy, the silver Claret Jug pitcher has been presented annually to The Open Championship winner since 1873.
